dedupe_keys.name: california emergency department data hcai ed visits and admissions by facility and ed visits per treatment station as a measure of ed burden

description: These two data sets measure how busy each California hospital's emergency department is and how much room it has to treat patients. They are published by the California Department of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI), formerly the Office of Statewide Health Planning and Development, on the state's health and human services open data portal. The volume and capacity file gives, for each hospital and year from 2021 to 2023, the number of ED encounters, the number of treatment stations and the ratio of visits per station as an indicator of ED burden, with a data dictionary. The encounters file gives counts of ED visits and of visits that led to admission, by facility and year. Coverage is licensed hospitals with emergency departments across California. Both are free and available to download as Excel or CSV. Caveats: the portal states no licence, figures are annual totals, not hourly arrivals, and hospitals must be linked to locations through their facility identifiers. Simulation uses: setting baseline ED demand and station capacity for surge and disaster scenarios such as wildfire smoke or heat events, and identifying crowded departments. Related records: the HCAI annual utilisation and financial data (data-hcai-hospital-utilization-and-financial), which also includes ED service trends, and the California COVID-19 hospital capacity data (data-california-covid19-hospital-capacity-by-county).
